investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource required by the pod but reported it as exhausted (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm); the other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the two eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the four affinity-mismatched nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~146 s before the eval timed out, the agent VM was never created, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were never written, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: the cluster has only 2 nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector and expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, and all available VM slots on those nodes are currently consumed by other running remote-agent pods or workloads.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's affinity rules target only 2 of 6 nodes, leaving 4 nodes permanently ineligible regardless of their resource availability. If the intended pool was larger, a misconfigured label or selector would explain the narrow scheduling target.

Tertiary — cluster capacity not scaled to meet demand: the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may have a fixed or under-provisioned VM slot quota that has not been increased to match the current eval or workload concurrency.

Lower probability — transient resource spike: a burst of concurrent remote-agent provisioning requests (e.g., from parallel eval runs or user traffic) temporarily exhausted the VM slots, and capacity would recover once existing agents are cleaned up.

If the remote-agent pod spec does not actually request kata.peerpods.io/vm (i.e., the scheduler message is from a different pod), the diagnosis would need to be revised.
If more than 2 nodes carry the required node affinity label (i.e., the 4/6 split is incorrect), the affinity-restriction hypothesis would be weakened.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after cleanup of existing remote-agent pods succeeds and produces all four evidence fields, the cause is confirmed as transient resource exhaustion rather than a permanent misconfiguration.
If no other pods are consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the eligible nodes, the exhaustion would point to a quota or capacity configuration error rather than competing workloads.

If the eval history shows this check was passing recently with the same cluster size, a recent workload increase or leaked pod accumulation would be the more likely cause than a structural misconfiguration.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-02T04:34–04:39Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written — causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail with all four required evidence fields missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent eval environment has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 preemption victims available and no schedulable node, the eval pod remained Unschedulable for ~144s before the check timed out. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so this is an eval-level failure, not a confirmed user-facing outage.

[Secondary] Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, artificially constraining scheduling to only 2 nodes and making capacity exhaustion more likely.

[Less likely] Transient cluster-level resource pressure: a concurrent workload spike may have consumed all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, which could self-resolve.
[Less likely] Eval environment configuration issue: the eval pod's resource requests or node selector may be overly restrictive, preventing scheduling on nodes that could otherwise accommodate it.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource required by the pod but reported it as exhausted (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm); the other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the two eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the four affinity-mismatched nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~146 s before the eval timed out, the agent VM was never created, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were never written, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: the cluster has only 2 nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector and expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, and all available VM slots on those nodes are currently consumed by other running remote-agent pods or workloads.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's affinity rules target only 2 of 6 nodes, leaving 4 nodes permanently ineligible regardless of their resource availability. If the intended pool was larger, a misconfigured label or selector would explain the narrow scheduling target.

Tertiary — cluster capacity not scaled to meet demand: the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may have a fixed or under-provisioned VM slot quota that has not been increased to match the current eval or workload concurrency.

Lower probability — transient resource spike: a burst of concurrent remote-agent provisioning requests (e.g., from parallel eval runs or user traffic) temporarily exhausted the VM slots, and capacity would recover once existing agents are cleaned up.

With 0 preemption victims available and no schedulable node, the eval pod remained Unschedulable for ~144s before the check timed out. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so this is an eval-level failure, not a confirmed user-facing outage.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place agent pods: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval probe never reached the stage of creating an agent or receiving a runtime response, so all required evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is absent and the expected-output contract is entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. At the time of the eval run, 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new remote-agent pod: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported it as fully consumed, and the other 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable on both eligible nodes. Because pod scheduling failed, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1918) never completed, no evidence was collected, and the eval timed out after ~142–146 seconds across all three checks. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes in the production-api cluster, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. All three sibling checks share this exact scheduler message, confirming a cluster-wide capacity ceiling rather than a single-pod anomaly (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary: The node affinity/selector on remote-agent pods restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes. If those nodes are at capacity, there is no fallback — the 4 remaining nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of their general resource availability (failed-check.message: '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector').

Tertiary: A concurrent workload spike or leaked/stuck remote-agent pods from a prior eval run may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes, preventing preemption because no lower-priority victims exist (failed-check.message: 'No preemption victims found for incoming pod').

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity in the production-api cluster to determine whether the resource is still exhausted. If so, scale up the number of kata-capable nodes or increase the vm resource limit on existing nodes to restore scheduling headroom.
Audit all pods currently holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations, particularly any in Terminating or long-running states from prior eval runs, and force-delete any leaked pods to free capacity.
Re-run the three remote-agents eval checks after capacity is confirmed available to verify the evals return to passing status and all required evidence fields are populated.

Review the node affinity/selector configuration on remote-agent pods to determine whether the restriction to only 2 kata-capable nodes is intentional. If additional nodes can be made kata-capable, this would provide scheduling redundancy and prevent a single-node saturation event from failing all remote-agent checks simultaneously.

Investigate whether preemption policy can be configured for remote-agent eval pods so that lower-priority workloads can be evicted when eval capacity is needed, reducing the risk of future scheduling deadlocks.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is available and unallocated on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the root cause is not resource exhaustion and another scheduling constraint must be investigated.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure window succeeds and returns all required evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message), the exhaustion was transient and likely caused by a concurrent workload rather than a persistent capacity ceiling.

If the scheduler message changes on re-run to a different error (e.g., image pull failure, API authentication error, or network timeout), the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion was a coincidental condition and the true root cause lies elsewhere.
If only remote-agent-runtime fails while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state pass on a subsequent run, the failure is isolated to the runtime check and not a shared scheduling constraint.

If no pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time of investigation, the resource may have been temporarily over-reported as exhausted due to a node status sync lag rather than actual allocation.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and allocatable headroom on all eligible nodes, alerting before the resource is fully exhausted rather than after scheduling fails.

Add a check that detects stuck or leaked remote-agent pods (e.g., pods in Terminating state for more than a configurable threshold) and reports them as a warning before they exhaust scheduling capacity.

Add a pre-flight scheduling check to the remote-agent eval runner that verifies at least one kata.peerpods.io/vm slot is available before attempting createAgent, and returns a distinct SKIP or WARN status with a descriptive message rather than timing out after 142+ seconds.
Consider adding a historical baseline eval that tracks kata.peerpods.io/vm utilization over time so that capacity trends can be detected before they cause eval failures.
